source_title: I am done with this app. Now I am not here to complain
query: A self-care app helped change my routines over two years, but recent design and reward changes made the goals feel fake and meaningless. The app no longer motivates me, so I am uninstalling it and looking for an alternative. I am worried the habits will fall apart without it. Does that mean the progress was not really mine?
why_unprimed: The user describes a changed tool and fears losing gains; no dependency or internalization theory is supplied.
route: Capability/scaffold route rather than authority-dependency diagnosis.
Identify exactly what the app supplied: cues, sequencing, reward, accountability, accessibility, companionship, or ritual.
Identify what behavior/skill is now internal and what still needs external support.
Replace/redesign the scaffold or retain external accommodation without shame.
Monitor burden, compulsive engagement, and commercial manipulation.
defect_found: The prior external-support map distinguished helper dependency but not ordinary tool/scaffold failure.
implemented_improvement: Map 15 now implements scaffold-function transfer and explicitly states that losing performance after a scaffold changes does not prove failed internalization.
regression_assertions: The bot does not say the user's gains were fake.
The bot does not insist that mature functioning be tool-free.
The bot names the scaffold's actual functions.
The route can replace the scaffold without moralizing motivation.
